info.bio: Wild Cherry fue una banda de Rock estadounidense de la década de los 70 formada en Ohio. Destacó por su estilo Rock, Funk y R&B. Su mejor hit fue en el año 1976, con la canción "Play that funky music", canción interpretada en 1990 por el rapero Vanilla Ice.

scenes.name: El funk de los blancos: Average White Band y Wild Cherry
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: La Average White Band, escoceses blancos, firmó uno de los discos más funky de 1975, «Pick Up the Pieces» (con la guitarra de «Hot Pants Road» de los JB’s), y maduró hasta el funk introspectivo de Soul Searching; «School Boy Crush» acabó en temas de Eric B. & Rakim o Too Short. Pero cuando los blancos tocan música negra todo se complica: AWB no tenía raíces de blues ni Motown que la anclaran; Grand Funk Railroad tenía actitud funky pero no el groove; KC and the Sunshine Band pasaba por banda negra; Wild Cherry, de los bares rockeros de Pittsburgh, llegó al número 1 R&B con «Play That Funky Music» (1976). Que el único número 1 funk que suena en la radio rock sea de blancos dice mucho de raza en América.

podcast.title: Appearance on Dina (1976)
podcast.body: Wild Cherry appeared on Dina Shore's talk show on November 26, 1976, as part of an episode that also featured comedian George Kirby, Miss Teenage America Kathy Jordan, singer Lynn Anderson, and ABBA. This appearance helped expose the band to a more mature audience. "The November 26 1976 episode of Dina featured the comedian George Kirby the band wild cherry Miss Teenage America Kathy Jordan singer Lynn Anderson who sang Rose Garden."

podcast.title: Funk Rock Categorization
podcast.body: Hailing from Steubenville, Ohio, Wild Cherry is often categorized as a funk rock band, a label influenced by their race as much as their music. "Wild Cherry, a band from Stubenville, Ohio... Are often categorized as a funk rock band, a label that has as much to do with their race as their music."

podcast.title: One-Hit Wonder Status
podcast.body: Despite having a successful song with "Play That Funky Music," Wild Cherry was unable to replicate that success with follow-up singles, ultimately becoming a one-hit wonder. "I mean they had a great song with play that funky music but they could never replicate that."
